name: code-coach-vscode
description: Finds 30 kinds of beginner Java logic mistakes as you type, and coaches you to fix them yourself

codeCoach.backendUrl.description: Where the extension calls Code Coach's API. The default is the deployed Code Guru platform. Developers running the compose stack use http://localhost:8090; the backend on its own under uvicorn is http://127.0.0.1:8000. Keep it on the same host as Portal URL.

codeCoach.enableEvaluationLogging.description: Send anonymized diagnostic events to Code Coach for research evaluation logging. Off by default.

codeCoach.portalUrl.description: The Code Guru web app. Sign In and Create Account open its /login and /register pages in your browser, and the session comes back to VS Code automatically. The default is the deployed platform; the compose stack serves it at http://localhost:8090, and `npm run dev` at http://localhost:4200.

codeCoach.autoAnalyze.description: Check the Java file automatically when you pause typing. Off: only when you run Code Coach: Analyze Current File.

codeCoach.analysisDelayMs.description: How long Code Coach waits after you stop typing before checking the file, in milliseconds.

codeCoach.mutedErrorTypes.description: Kinds of finding not to show in the editor, by id (for example NON_SHORT_CIRCUIT_OPERATOR). Use 'Mute this kind' in the Coach Panel to add one.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Code Coach
walkthroughs.description: Code Coach helps beginner Java programmers learn from their mistakes with progressive hints and targeted feedback powered by ML.

steps.title: Sign In or Create an Account
steps.description:
Code Coach tracks your learning progress. Sign in to save your sessions and get personalized feedback.

[Sign In](command:code-coach-vscode.signIn) or [Create Account](command:code-coach-vscode.createAccount)

media.altText: Sign in screen with lock icon and authentication buttons

steps.title: Open a Java File
steps.description:
Code Coach works with Java source files. Open any `.java` file in your workspace to begin — your own assignment, a practice exercise, or any Java project.

Code Coach will automatically detect supported files.

media.altText: VS Code editor with a Java file open showing code

steps.title: Analyze Your Code
steps.description:
Code Coach checks your Java for **30 kinds of beginner logic mistakes** - loops that stop one element early, a total reset inside its loop, `&` where `&&` was meant, else-if tests in the wrong order, and more. Most are judged by machine-learning models trained on code that was actually run.

[Analyze Current File](command:code-coach-vscode.analyzeCurrentFile)

Code Coach also runs **automatically** as you type, with results appearing after a brief pause.

media.altText: Magnifying glass analyzing code with results showing 3 issues found

steps.title: Explore Progressive Hints
steps.description:
Each issue comes with **3 levels of hints** that progressively guide you to the answer:

- 💡 **Concept** — explains the underlying idea
- 🧭 **Guidance** — points you in the right direction
- 🎯 **Targeted** — quotes your own code and asks the question that leads to the fix

Still stuck? **✨ Explain in my code** walks through your own lines with an example, **📘 Similar example** shows the same mistake fixed, and **🎓 Learn this** opens the free course unit. Code that does not compile yet? Code Coach explains the compiler's message in plain words too.

media.altText: Three progressive hint blocks in blue, teal, and purple

steps.title: Use the Coach Panel
steps.description:
The Coach Panel is your command center. Click the **🎓 graduation cap** icon in the activity bar (left sidebar) to open it.

Navigate between issues, view all hints at a glance, and track your session.

[Open Coach Panel](command:code-coach-vscode.openCoachPanel)

media.altText: Sidebar panel showing issue navigation and hint cards with editor warnings

scripts.pretest: npm run compile && npm run lint
